reward.title: The Coffee Cherry
reward.summary: The fruit of the coffee plant. Two seeds inside each one.
reward.fact: Cherries ripen unevenly on the same branch — pickers return three or four times.

reward.title: The Bean Belt
reward.summary: The equatorial band where coffee grows — and why place ends up in the cup.
reward.fact: The same variety planted in two countries can taste completely different. Origin does the talking.

reward.title: Arabica
reward.summary: The species behind most specialty coffee. Sweet, nuanced, fragile.
reward.fact: Every arabica plant traces back to a small founding population in Ethiopia — the genetic diversity is unusually narrow.

reward.title: Beans Field Guide
reward.summary: Arabica or Robusta, where it grew, how it was processed.
reward.fact: That coffee bag isn’t just labels anymore — you know what they mean.

reward.title: The Drying Bed
reward.summary: Where the choice gets made — fruit on, fruit off, or somewhere between.
reward.fact: On a raised bed, cherries are turned by hand every few hours so they dry evenly and never ferment too far.

reward.title: Fermentation
reward.summary: The quiet chemistry that turns leftover fruit sugar into flavour.
reward.fact: A few extra hours of fermentation can be the difference between clean citrus and full-on blueberry.

reward.title: The Coffee Label
reward.summary: Origin, variety, process, roast date — four lines that predict your cup.
reward.fact: Read enough labels and you’ll guess the taste before the first sip more often than not.

reward.title: The Roast Spectrum
reward.summary: Light to dark — how far the heat goes, and what it trades away.
reward.fact: Roast level barely changes caffeine — it mostly trades origin acidity for roast flavour.

reward.title: First and Second Crack
reward.summary: The two sounds that tell a roaster how far a roast has gone.
reward.fact: First crack sounds like faint popcorn; second crack is sharper, like crackling.

reward.title: The Roast Date
reward.summary: The one number that tells you whether a bag is worth buying.
reward.fact: Most coffee is at its best from a few days to about a month after roasting.

reward.title: Particle Size
reward.summary: How coarse or fine you grind — the speed dial for extraction.
reward.fact: Halving particle size roughly doubles the surface the water can reach.

reward.title: Burr vs Blade
reward.summary: Why an even grind — not a fancy brewer — is the upgrade that counts.
reward.fact: Blade grinders make dust and boulders at once; burrs make one even size.

reward.title: The Grinder
reward.summary: Your first and best dial for fixing a cup that tastes off.
reward.fact: Baristas change grind before almost anything else — it moves the cup more than any other single tweak.

reward.title: The Brew Ratio
reward.summary: Coffee to water, by weight — the dial that sets your cup’s strength.
reward.fact: Most filter recipes live between 1:15 and 1:17. Pick one, weigh it, and stay consistent.

reward.title: Water
reward.summary: The invisible 98% — temperature and quality shape every cup.
reward.fact: Brewed coffee is about 98% water; filtered and just off the boil is the easy target.

reward.title: Sour vs Bitter
reward.summary: Two words that diagnose almost any bad cup.
reward.fact: Sour and thin means too little extraction; bitter and dry means too much. Everything else is a nudge back to the middle.

reward.title: Processing Field Guide
reward.summary: You can taste the difference between a washed and a natural coffee.
reward.fact: Washed, natural, honey — now you know why they matter.

reward.title: Roasting Field Guide
reward.summary: You can read a roast date and tell if a bag is still fresh.
reward.fact: Light, medium, dark — now you know what the roast is telling you.

reward.title: Grind Field Guide
reward.summary: You know how grind size and grinder type change the cup.
reward.fact: Coarse, medium, fine — now you know which way to turn the dial.

reward.title: Brew Field Guide
reward.summary: You can set a ratio, fix your water, and understand what went wrong.
reward.fact: You’re not just making coffee anymore — you know what changes the cup.

reward.title: Altitude
reward.summary: Why the number in metres on a bag predicts the cup.
reward.fact: Most specialty coffee grows between 1,200 and 2,200 metres — high enough to ripen slowly, low enough to avoid frost.

reward.title: The Trade
reward.summary: What the words on a bag promise, and who they promise it to.
reward.fact: Specialty is a score, not a vibe — 80 or more out of 100, cupped.

reward.title: The Cherry in Section
reward.summary: Skin, pulp, mucilage, parchment, silverskin, seed.
reward.fact: Around 80% of a picked cherry never leaves the farm — you brew the small hard bit in the middle.

cards.lessonTitle: Inside the cherry, layer by layer

reward.title: Varieties
reward.summary: Typica, Bourbon, Geisha — the names behind the cup.
reward.fact: Almost every Arabica grown today traces back to Typica or Bourbon.

reward.title: Drying
reward.summary: The slow step that decides whether a lot survives the journey.
reward.fact: Sun drying takes 10–25 days, and naturals run longest because the fruit is still on.

reward.title: Anaerobic Fermentation
reward.summary: The stage where much of the flavour is actually made.
reward.fact: Seal the tank and starve it of oxygen, and the same cherry tastes like a different fruit.

reward.title: Decaf
reward.summary: How the caffeine comes out, and what stays behind.
reward.fact: Roughly 97% removed is the bar — a decaf cup still carries a few milligrams.

reward.title: The Roast
reward.summary: What heat actually does to a green bean.
reward.fact: First crack arrives around 195–205 °C, when steam pressure pops the bean open.

reward.title: Light vs Dark
reward.summary: Two ends of the spectrum, and how to choose between them.
reward.fact: Caffeine survives roasting — light roasts only win by the scoop because dark beans are less dense.

cards.lessonTitle: Light vs dark, side by side

reward.title: Caffeine
reward.summary: How much is really in the cup in front of you.
reward.fact: A single espresso carries less caffeine than a mug of drip — concentration is not dose.

cards.lessonTitle: How much caffeine are you actually drinking?

reward.title: Grind and Brewer
reward.summary: Which grind belongs to which brewer, and why.
reward.fact: The longer the water sits with the coffee, the coarser the grind has to be.

reward.title: Freshness
reward.summary: Aroma escaping is what you smell — and flavour you will never taste. Peak flavour holds:
reward.fact: Grinding multiplies the exposed surface enormously — staling starts immediately.

cards.lessonTitle: Why pre-ground never tastes as good

reward.title: Your Grinder
reward.summary: What the money actually buys in a grinder.
reward.fact: A hand burr grinder usually out-grinds an electric at the same price.

reward.title: Extraction
reward.summary: How much of the coffee actually made it into the water.
reward.fact: Only about 30% of a bean can dissolve at all — and you want 18–22% of the bean’s weight in the cup.

reward.title: The Filter
reward.summary: Paper, metal or cloth — and what each one keeps out of the cup.
reward.fact: Paper traps the oils that carry body; metal lets them straight through.

reward.title: The Shot
reward.summary: Why nine bars makes a different drink out of the same coffee.
reward.fact: Espresso is a method, not a roast: ~9 bars for ~28 seconds, 18 g in and about 36 g out, with crema on top.

reward.title: Your First Cup
reward.summary: Every decision in the course, assembled into one brew.
reward.fact: Weighing the water matters as much as weighing the coffee — most people only do half.
